Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

well done phrase

praise

also good job, you carried that well, encouragement, you did fine, good for you, oh boy!, good!, bravo!, good going!

classical

Traupman 322
Liv. II 12, 14
Cic. Att. XII 6, 3
Verg. Aen. IX 641: macte novā virtūte, puer
Traupman 99: macte virtūte estō!
Traupman 43
Traupman 193: Macte virtūte estō!, good for you!

Macte virtūte!

The final e of macte is short.

Other words

  • euge

    classical

    An interjection of approval.

  • Bene factum!

    also used · classical · Traupman 99; Traupman 99; Traupman 322

  • Rēctē factum!

    also used · modern · Traupman 101; Traupman 101; Traupman 322; Traupman 335

  • Pulchrē, bene, rēctē! — praise for a finished result

    also used · classical · Hor. Ars 428

  • Tū decus omne tuīs. — you are the pride of your family

    also used · classical · Verg. Ecl. 5, 34

    Said to the cook.

  • Eu! — good! well done! (also ironic)

    interjection · also used · classical · Hor. Ars 327–330: eu! rem poteris servāre tuam; Traupman 105: oh boy!, eu!

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Hor.)

    Greek εὖ, “well!”: praise for a right answer, or, in comedy, mock praise. Stronger is euge!.

Examples

  • Bene portāvistī.

    You carried that well.composed

  • Bene factum!

    Well done!composed

  • Pulchrē, bene, rēctē!

    praise for a finished result: Dad over the pies, in Horace’s words (Ars 428)composed

  • Pater puerum Rōmānōrum illud «Macte virtūte!» docuerat; quod igitur Baba Bulgaricē dīcit, puer ipse sibi Latīnē.

    Dad had taught the boy the Roman “Macte virtūte!”; so what Baba says in Bulgarian, the boy says to himself in Latin.composed

  • Cui pater «Rēctē factum!» inquit.

    Dad said to him, “Well done!”composed

  • Euge, Theodōre.

    Well done, Theo.composed

  • Fēcistī probē.

    You did fine.Traupman 98

  • sī dē quīncūnce remōta est ūncia, quid superat? … — triēns. — eu! rem poteris servāre tuam.

    If a twelfth is taken from five twelfths, what is left? — A third. — Good! You’ll be able to look after your money.Hor. Ars 327–330

See also job, help.
